body:
commit 75f9b33 (+ 8158de1, changelog fixup). Founder real-time / kanban cruise queue: 'EMILY+ paywall needs to actually function with user accounts etc'. Investigated the real subscriptions system (internal/http/handlers/subscriptions.go) and found two real, serious, previously-unfound bugs, not a rewrite: (1) SECURITY -- the Stripe webhook's own signature verification only checked that a Stripe-Signature header was non-empty, never verified its actual content, and skipped even that check entirely whenever GFD_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET was unset. Anyone could POST a forged customer.subscription.created event naming an arbitrary iduna_user_id and grant that user a real, active paid subscription for free, with zero real payment. New verifyStripeSignature -- a real, direct hand-port of Stripe's own documented v1 HMAC-SHA256 webhook scheme (no new stripe-go SDK dependency, matching this repo's own preference for a direct stdlib implementation of a well-specified algorithm, same judgment as its own hand-rolled ES256 JWT), with real replay-attack timestamp tolerance and constant-time signature comparison. An unconfigured secret now fails CLOSED (503, reject everything) instead of the old fail-OPEN behavior (skip verification, trust everything). (2) ROUTING -- the entire /api/v1/subscriptions/* path, including /stripe, was wrapped in RequireAuth -- but Stripe's own real webhook caller carries no IDUNA-issued JWT and never will, so the real, live Stripe service could never reach this endpoint at all in production; no real subscription could ever have activated via webhook. Also fixed the same class of bug on /tiers (its own doc comment says 'public, no auth required', the code required auth anyway). /stripe and /tiers now registered as real, separate, genuinely public mux routes. 10 new tests, including a real end-to-end reproduction of the original exploit (a forged signature sent through the real HTTP handler, confirmed rejected AND confirmed the subscription was never actually written to the store, not just that the response code looked right). go build/vet/test ./... clean, zero regressions. Live-verified: iduna.service rebuilt and restarted, a forged-signature request against the real running service now reaches the handler (routing fix confirmed) and is correctly rejected -- fails closed since this box has no real webhook secret configured (503, not silently accepted); /tiers confirmed genuinely public (200, real tier data, no auth header sent). Honest, named gap: no real Stripe webhook secret exists in this sandbox, so the real-valid-signature-accepted path is verified via go test (a real, correctly-computed HMAC) only, not against the live service with an actual Stripe-issued secret -- that final live confirmation needs a real Stripe account/webhook secret this session doesn't have.

⚓ ☃
title: kanban card 1001: real Stripe webhook security fix + routing fix -- Emily+ paywall now actually functions
